title: Machine execution matches transducer semantics
statement: Let $S$ be a finite state set with decidable equality, let $\delta:S\times\{0,1\}\to S$ be a transition function, let $\varepsilon:S\times\{0,1\}\to\{0,1\}\cup\{\text{no output}\}$ be a per-bit emission rule, let $\phi:S\to\{0,1\}\cup\{\text{no output}\}$ be a final emission rule, and choose a start state. For Boolean words $x$ and $r$, suppose $x=p\mathbin{++}r$ for a word $p$; for every state $q$ and already-emitted word $o$, the associated transducer machine, started on input $x$ in state $q$ with its input head at position $|p|$ and output $o$, is halted after $|r|+1$ steps and has output $o$ followed by the transducer semantics on $q$ and $r$.
hypotheses_covered: The state set has decidable equality
A transition function on states and bits

Let the input decompose as $x = p \mathbin{+\!\!+} r$. From any state $q$ at
position $|p|$ with emitted prefix $o$, the word-transducer machine halts after
